title: Donkey Kong Was Built to Empty a Warehouse of Failed Arcade Cabinets
hook: In 1980 Nintendo was stuck with about 2,000 unsold Radar Scope arcade cabinets in America. A young artist named Shigeru Miyamoto designed a game to fill them: Donkey Kong. This week he was named the first ever Legend Award winner at the D.I.C.E. Awards. Which Miyamoto game is your favorite?
script: Did you know Donkey Kong only exists because Nintendo was stuck with two thousand unsold arcade machines? In 1980 Nintendo shipped three thousand cabinets of a game called Radar Scope to America. Only about a thousand of them sold. The rest sat in Nintendo's American warehouse, and the company needed a way to use them. President Hiroshi Yamauchi ordered a new game built to fit inside those old cabinets. The design that won came from a young staff artist named Shigeru Miyamoto, who had joined Nintendo in 1977. He first asked to make a Popeye game, but Nintendo could not use the license. So Miyamoto invented his own characters instead. A giant ape, a lady named Pauline, and a hero simply called Jumpman. Donkey Kong came out in 1981 and became one of the biggest arcade hits of its era. Jumpman was later renamed Mario, after the landlord of Nintendo's American office. And this week, the Academy of Interactive Arts and Sciences named Miyamoto the first ever winner of its Legend Award. The academy says it will hand out that honor no more than once a decade. Not bad for a game built to empty a warehouse. Which Miyamoto game is your favorite? Follow for more gaming history.
